Definition: from Εὖρος (the east wind) and G2830; a storm from the East (or southeast), i.e. (in modern phrase) a Levanter:--Euroklydon.
BiblicalUsage: Euroklydon is the name of the tempestuous wind that struck Paul's ship, and it stands in Acts 27:14, where the wind called Euroclydon beat against the island of Crete. The verse is a Textus Receptus reading: the SBL text at Acts 27:14 reads Euraquilo instead, the same storm under a different name.
TheologicalSignificance: I take Euroklydon as it stands: a storm from the East.
RelatedTopics: Nature and Creation; God's Power; God's Providence
